newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for Sunday in the English premier league (kick-off times 1500 GMT, league positions in parentheses):
Aston Villa (5) v Southampton (16)

Aston Villa need only one point to guarantee themselves a place in European competition next season while Southampton require a point to ensure premier league safety. Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich (knee injury) and midfielder Mark Draper (hamstring) will undergo late fitness tests.
Southampton, unbeaten in seven games, see the return of defender Jason Dodd from suspension while defender Claus Lundekvam is doubtful with a shoulder injury.
Blackburn Rovers (13) v Leicester City (12)

Blackburn gained the vital point they needed for survival when they drew with Middlesbrough on Thursday and will go into next season with a new manager, Roy Hodgson from Inter Milan. Strikers Per Pedersen and Chris Sutton are both doubtful with hamstring injuries.
Leicester beat Sheffield Wednesday 1-0 to guarantee their place in the premier league next season.
Derby County (10) v Arsenal (4)
Derby coach Jim Smith could welcome back Croatian defender Igor Stimac from a long-term back injury in an otherwise unchanged line-up from last week's 2-1 win at Coventry.

Arsenal are assured a UEFA Cup place for next season as coach Arsene Wenger plans changes to an ageing side over the summer period. Wenger will send out the same line-up as the one which lost 1-0 to Newcastle last week.
Everton (15) v Chelsea (6)

Everton have been assured premier league safety after favourable results in other matches this week but caretaker coach Dave Watson will be without defenders David Unsworth (suspension) and Craig Short (neck injury). Irish defender Terry Phelan and strikers Michael Branch and Graham Stuart will undergo late fitness tests.

Chelsea have a chance, if they win, to earn a European place through the league. Coach Ruud Gullit's doubts are defenders Steve Clarke and Eddie Newton as he prepares for next weekend's F.A. Cup final against Middlesbrough.
Leeds United (11) v Middlesbrough (18)

Coach George Graham's fully fit squad have lost twice in their last eight games but have not conceded a league goal at home this year. They take on a Middlesbrough side desperate for victory to give them any chance of premier league survival.

Middlesbrough, who drew 0-0 at Blackburn on Thursday, face their fourth match in eight days. Coach Bryan Robson could welcome back Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli, while Ben Roberts will continue in goal.
Manchester United (1) v West Ham United (14)

Manchester United were crowned champions for the fourth time in five seasons after Liverpool and Newcastle failed to win their midweek matches. Coach Alex Ferguson's only major doubt is Welsh midfielder Ryan Giggs who was missing from Thursday's goalless draw against Newcastle.

West Ham's run of 12 games with only two losses has been enough to assure the London side of premier league football for next season. Coach Harry Redknapp will add midfielder John Moncur to an injury list which includes captain Julian Dicks.
Newcastle (3) v Nottingham Forest (20)

Newcastle need to win and hope that Liverpool lose if they are to finish second and earn the remaining place in the European Cup next season. England midfielder Robert Lee, who has a calf strain, and unsettled winger David Ginola, who faces a fitness test on a knee injury, are coach Kenny Dalglish's only worries.

Forest player/coach Stuart Pearce will make his last first-team selection on Sunday after he announced on Thursday that he was stepping down to concentrate on his playing career. Pearce is rated extremely doubtful for the game as Alan Fettis continues in goal for hernia victim Mark Crossley. Dave Bassett will take control of all first-team management matters as from Monday.
Sheffield Wednesday (7) v Liverpool (2)

Sheffield Wednesday, who beat Liverpool 1-0 in the reverse fixture, have lost their last three games away but have the best home record, with only one loss all season. Coach David Pleat goes into the final game of the season without long-term absentees Jon Newsome and Graham Hyde.

Liverpool could face the prospect of the second European Cup place being decided to their detriment on goal difference if they draw and Newcastle, three goals ahead of the Anfield side, win. Roy Evans's side lost to Wimbledon on Tuesday and are without striker Robbie Fowler.
Tottenham Hotspur (9) v Coventry City (19)

Tottenham coach Gerry Francis will give Norwegian under-21 goalkeeper Espen Baardsen his full debut for the club in place of the injured Ian Walker. Both Walker and England international Darren Anderton have been told to rest for six weeks to recover from injuries.

Coventry must win and hope that other results go their way if they are to stand any chance of survival. Player/coach Gordon Strachan and defender David Burrows both face late fitness tests on hamstring injuries.
Wimbledon (8) v Sunderland (17)

Wimbledon ended Liverpool's title hopes with a 2-1 win on Tuesday for only their second victory in the last 13 games. Coach Joe Kinnear will have to decide whether to play doubtful midfielder Robbie Earle or Peter Fear.
Sunderland need to win their third game in four outings to retain their top-flight status. Coach Peter Reid will be without defenders Andy Melville (Achilles injury) and Martin Scott (leg).
